summary: Salmaan Faarsi invited the Persians of a besieged fortress to Islaam for three days before his army attacked.
Salmaan Faarsi was appointed to invite the people of Bahursher and Qasrul Abyadh to Islaam, giving each three days, as Atiyya reports.
notes: Atiyya is not in the approved list; his Companion status is not clear from the text.

summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas sent a group of senior Sahabah to invite Rustam to Islaam before the Battle of Qaadisiyyah, and they told him they were sure Allaah would give them his lands.
notes: Text stops mid-dream, after 'handed them over to Hadhrat Umar'.

summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba explained Islaam to Rustam, the Persian commander, before the Battle of Qaadisiyyah, and Rustam asked questions about it.
Rib'ee bin Aamir, sent by Sa'd, invited Rustam to Islaam in his court and refused his request for more than three days to decide.
On the second and third days Hudhayfa bin Mihsin and Mughiera bin Shu'ba presented Islaam to Rustam, who answered with a parable and threatened to kill them all.
notes: Continues the Rustam account begun in the previous narration.

summary: Before the Battle of Qaadisiyyah Mughiera bin Shu'ba went to Rustam, mocked the Persians' taunts, and presented Islaam and Jizya, and the Muslims then defeated the Persians at the river crossing.
notes: The text says the Kuffaar army figure is from 'a narration of Hadhrat (RA)' with the name missing (OCR); no person tagged for it.

summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba was sent to the Persian leader before Qaadisiyyah and told him the Muslims had come to call to Islaam and to fight, not for food.
notes: Mu'aawiya bin Qurra is labelled RA in the text but his Companion status is not clear from it.

summary: Sa'd's envoys, led by Nu'maan bin Muqarrin and Mughiera bin Shu'ba, invited the Persian king Yazdajird to Islaam before the battle, and Mughiera answered his threats.
notes: The '(1)' footnote text inside the narration is OCR debris and was ignored.

summary: Abdullaah bin Mu'tam invited the Arab tribes of Taghlib, Iyaad and Namir to testify to the Kalimah and accept what the Prophet brought, and they accepted Islaam.
notes: The narrator line reads 'Hadhrat Muhammad ﷺ, Hadhrat Talha (RA)'; the first name is probably an OCR error, so it is not tagged as a narrator.

summary: Amr bin Al Aas offered the Egyptian priests Islaam or Jizya before the battle for Egypt, and after a night attack the Egyptians came out to negotiate at Aynush Shams.
notes: Khaalid and Ubaadah are not identified in the text, so they are not matched to approved entries. The Egyptian chief priest Abu Maryam here may not be the Abu Maryam of n00218.

summary: Umar appointed Salama bin Qais Ash'jaee as commander of a regiment and told him to offer the enemy Islaam, then Jizya, and only then fight.
notes: Ends with 'The narration continues in great detail', so the report is cut off.

summary: Abu Moosa Ash'ari invited the people of Isfahan to Islaam and then offered Jizya, but they broke the night's agreement and attacked, and the Muslims were given victory.
notes: The narrator name reads 'Bau Umayya' in the text, probably an OCR error for Abu Umayya.

summary: Amr bin Jamooh, who kept an idol, was won over when the young Muslims of Banu Salma repeatedly disgraced it, and he then accepted Islaam.
notes: Two men are named Mu'aadh here (Mu'aadh bin Jabal and Amr's son Mu'aadh); both are recorded separately.

summary: Amr bin Jamooh's son recited the opening verses of the Qur'aan to his father, who consulted his idol, broke it, and accepted Islaam.
notes: Contains the family report, the idol-breaking, and a second narration with couplets. The son is not named in this text; he is identified from n00214.

summary: Abdullaah bin Rawwaaha smashed Abu Dardaa's idol, and Abu Dardaa, seeing that it could not defend itself, went to the Prophet and accepted Islaam.
Umar's letter to Amr bin Al Aas set the terms for Alexandria's Jizya and for the prisoners, who were to be offered Islaam or their own religion.
After the prisoners of Alexandria were each offered Islaam or Christianity, Abdullaah bin Abdur Rahmaan, known as Abu Maryam, accepted Islaam despite his family's opposition.
notes: Continues the Ziyaad bin Jaz report from the previous narration. The text reads 'Arrtr' for Amr bin Al Aas (OCR). It is not stated whether this Abu Maryam is the Egyptian chief priest of n00211, so they are not merged.

summary: Ali's armour was found with a Christian, and when the judge Shuray ruled that Ali needed proof, the Christian accepted Islaam and Ali gave him the armour.
notes: The Prophet's words are quoted by Ali (about non-Muslims in a Muslim country).

summary: Ali's armour was found with a Jew, the judge Shuray refused Ali's son Hasan's testimony, and the Jew, persuaded by Ali's honesty, accepted Islaam and was given the armour with money.
notes: Combines two reports (Haakim's and Yazeed Tameemi's). The text reads 'Urnar' for Umar (OCR). The Prophet is quoted saying Hasan and Husayn are leaders of the youth of Jannah.

summary: Jareer reports the conditions the male Sahabah pledged to the Prophet, which matched those the women pledged, with the promise of Jannah for keeping them.
notes: The text gives only 'Jareer'. It is probably Jareer bin Abdillaah but this is not confirmed.

summary: Aswad saw people pledge to Islaam and the Shahaadah on the day of the Conquest of Makkah, and his teacher explained what the Shahaadah required.
notes: Aswad and the two named teachers are not in the approved list and their Companion status is not clear from the text.

summary: Bayhaqi reports that people of every age and both sexes pledged to Islaam and the Shahaadah at the Prophet's hands.
Mujaashi bin Mas'ood asked to pledge to Hijrah after the conquest, and the Prophet instead took his pledge to Islaam and Jihaad, since Hijrah had ended.
notes: His brother is mentioned only in the heading; he is not named in the text, so is not tagged.

summary: After Mughiera bin Shu'ba died, Jareer bin Abdillaah urged the people to fear Allaah and wish well for every Muslim, and Ziyaad bin Haarith Sudaa'ee's pledge to Islaam is also recorded.
notes: Two reports: Jareer's address (relayed by Ziyaad bin Ilaaqa) and Ziyaad bin Haarith's pledge, plus a cross-reference to the Chapter of Da'wah. Jareer is identified from the heading as Jareer bin Abdillaah.

summary: Basheer bin Khasaasiyah asked, when pledging, to keep the conditions only as far as he was able, and this concession was allowed for everyone after him.
notes: The text is OCR-garbled at the Prophet's name and does not state the conditions; the heading's 'Sadaqah and Jihaad' is not supported by this text, so it is not tagged.

summary: Awf bin Maalik Ash'ja'ee and his companions pledged to worship Allaah alone, pray the five salaahs and never ask anyone for anything.
Thowbaan pledged to the Prophet never to ask anyone for anything, and Abu Umaamah reports him dismounting to pick up his own fallen whip, as Abu Bakr also did.
notes: Ends with a short second report about Abu Bakr.

summary: Abu Dharr reports the pledges he gave the Prophet: to fear no critic for Allaah's sake, never to ask anyone for anything, and never to accept a trust.
notes: Combines three reports (Abu Dharr's own account, Abul Muthanna's, and an 'another narration'). The end has OCR debris, which was ignored.

summary: Sahl bin Sa'd reports that Abu Dharr, Ubaadah bin Saamit, Abu Sa'eed Khudri, Muhammad bin Maslama and a sixth Sahabi pledged never to be swayed by critics in Allaah's cause, and the Prophet released the sixth when he asked.
notes: The opening sentence appears to be missing a verb (OCR), most likely 'narrates'.

summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit reports the pledge taken from Madinah's leaders: no shirk, theft, fornication, unlawful killing, plunder or disobedience, with Jannah promised for keeping it.
Ubaadah bin Saamit relays the Prophet's pledge against shirk, theft and fornication, and says that a sinner's fate is then left to Allaah's forgiveness or punishment.
notes: Trailing OCR debris after the report was ignored.

summary: Ubaadah bin Saamit reports that the eleven men of the first Aqaba pledge took the same pledge as the women, since jihaad was not yet obligatory, and renewed it the following year.
Ya'la bin Munyah asked to pledge his father to Hijrah after the conquest of Makkah, and the Prophet instead took a pledge of Jihaad because Hijrah had ended.
notes: Mujaashi and Jareer appear only as cross-references to earlier narrations. Footnote and OCR fragments were ignored.

summary: During the Battle of Khandaq the Prophet declined a Hijrah pledge from outside Madinah and praised the Ansaar, saying whoever loves them will be loved by Allaah.
notes: Two reports: Haarith bin Ziyaad's and Abu Usayd Saa'idi's. The text gives Howt's name two ways ('Howt bin Yazeed' or 'Yazeed bin Howt'), so his Companion status is unclear.

summary: Jaabir describes how the Prophet sought asylum at the Hajj markets, how the Ansaar of Yathrib offered it, and how seventy of them pledged at Aqaba to protect him.

Ka'b bin Maalik reports the Ansaar's pledge at Aqaba: Abbaas bin Abdil Muttalib asked for their commitment, Baraa bin Ma'roor took the Prophet's hand, and Abul Haytham bin Tayyihaan asked whether the Prophet would stay with them.
notes: Abbaas is recorded as not yet Muslim at the time, which the text itself states.

summary: Ka'b bin Maalik reports that the Prophet asked the Ansaar for twelve leaders to head their people, and they chose nine from Khazraj and three from Aws.
Urwa reports that Abul Haytham bin Tayyihaan was among the first to pledge, and after asking whether his people would help the Prophet, they all followed him.
notes: Ends with 'The Hadith continues further'. Urwa may be Urwa bin Zubayr, who was not a Companion; the text does not say which.

summary: Abbaas bin Ubaadah warned the Ansaar of the cost of the pledge before they took it for Jannah, and when he offered to attack Mina the Prophet said he had not been commanded to fight.
notes: The Abdullaah bin Ka'b here is not identified in the text and may not be the approved 'Abdullaah bin Ka'b bin Maalik'. Footnote references were ignored.
